title: Risk-adjusted intake matrix and sponsor-routing for enterprise model onboarding
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design and implement a risk-adjusted intake matrix and automated sponsor-routing for new model additions, version pin requests, and deprecation proposals from customers and internal teams. The matrix should combine quantifiable signals (SLA needs, data residency, compliance level, expected QPS, latency sensitivity, license risk, training data provenance, eval pass rate) with qualitative inputs (customer business criticality, legal/regulatory notes, strategic partner status). Outcome: consistent triage decisions and automated routing to the right reviewers (research, infra, security, enterprise solutions) plus a default timeline for eval gates, version pin approvals, and sunset windows based on risk tier.
acceptance_criteria: A documented intake matrix with weighted signals and scoring thresholds for Low/Medium/High/Blocked risk categories
Automation rules in the intake form that route submissions to the appropriate reviewers and mark required review types (security, legal, infra, ML research)
A decision playbook that maps score buckets to recommended outcomes: quick-approve, full-eval, version pin with guardrails, or defer/deprecate
Version-pinning flow with default TTLs (e.g., 90 days for P2, 365 days for P0 enterprise with SLA) and a manual override path including required approvers
Deprecation policy drafted: minimum notice, customer migration support checklist, and automated notification templates
Integration smoke-tests: new intake triggers a Jira/Linear ticket with correct labels and reviewer assignments, and populates a dashboard metric for intake-to-decision time
notes: Motivation: Customers are requesting ad-hoc version pinning and enterprise-specific model variants. Current triage is inconsistent and blocks adoption for regulated teams.
We need to balance speed (PLG onboarding) with risk controls for Dedicated/Private deployments.
Existing artifacts: model-intake form (Confluence), current catalog gating PRD, and recent enterprise intake interviews (see links).
Trade-offs: heavier gating slows onboarding but reduces downstream incidents; aim for automated low-friction paths for low-risk models.
Proposed scoring signals and initial weights are intentionally conservative; weights will be tuned in the first 6 weeks based on false positive/negative rate of gating decisions.
decisions: Adopt a numeric scoring model (0-100) instead of freeform tags to make routing thresholds deterministic
Initial weight distribution: Reliability/SLA 30, Data residency 20, Compliance (PII/regulated) 15, Eval pass/quality 15, License/IP risk 10, Customer criticality 10
High-risk models require both a security review and an infra readiness sign-off before being approved into Dedicated/Private
Version pin TTLs: default 90 days for P2-P3, 180 days for P1, 365 days for P0 (enterprise SLA) — can be shortened by infra if runtime compatibility issues are identified
Deprecation windows: minimum 45 days for low-impact models, 90 days for standard, 180+ days for enterprise tenants; migration assistance and export tools are required for enterprise deprecations
next_steps: Finalize intake form fields and implement weighted scoring logic (owner: PM)
Work with Engineering to support routing webhooks and reviewer assignment API (owner: Grant)
Draft security review checklist items for high-risk models (owner: Marta)
Prototype a dashboard metric for intake-to-decision time and rejection reasons (owner: Analytics)
Run a pilot with 5 incoming enterprise requests during Cycle 10 to validate thresholds and routing accuracy
